findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create ASN1Encoder instances and call write(...) whose results are discarded. These are no-ops that only add confusion; the actual encoding is done again at lines 117-121. Harmless functionally but indicates a copy/paste leftover that a maintainer would want removed.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER produces non-minimal/signed-incorrect DER integers
findings.body: r and s are built with a leading zero byte and passed to new BigInteger(r) then re-encoded via BigInteger.toByteArray(). This yields a correct minimal two's complement encoding, but the input is assumed to be unsigned big-endian of length signLength/2 with no check on signLength; if signLength is odd or the array is shorter than expected, System.arraycopy throws ArrayIndexOutOfBounds at runtime rather than a clear error. The method also never validates that signature.length >= signLength.

findings.title: readInteger uses signed BigInteger from DER without validation
findings.body: readInteger reads raw bytes and calls new BigInteger(bytes) which is correct for DER two's complement, but it does not reject empty content (length 0), which throws NumberFormatException instead of IOException, and readLength returning -1 (indefinite length) is passed directly to read(-1) causing NegativeArraySizeException. Malformed signatures from a server can therefore surface as unchecked exceptions.

findings.title: readSequence loop can run forever or miscount on zero-length elements
findings.body: In readSequence, the loop subtracts bytes.length from the remaining length per element. readNext returns header plus content; if the decoded length is inconsistent with the sequence, length may never reach zero or may go negative without error, and a malformed element with an indefinite-length marker (-1) is not rejected. Malformed input can cause misparsing or a hang risk rather than a clean IOException.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns a random keystore provider instead of a BC provider
findings.body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(default type).getProvider(), which is whatever provider supplies the default keystore (usually SUN/JKS), not BouncyCastle. Callers that expect BC (e.g. BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER lookups) get the wrong provider, and the method creates a keystore instance each call. Most other operations in this provider throw UnsupportedOperationException, so the BC provider mismatch is a real contract break for any code path that reaches it.

findings.title: order() of 100 makes the minimal provider win over full providers only if others are absent; CryptoIntegration selects by highest order
findings.body: CryptoIntegration sorts by order descending and picks the first. AuthzClientCryptoProvider has order 100 while DefaultCryptoProvider, Elytron and FIPS have 200, so they win when present. However, AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered via META-INF/services in the authz-client jar, and AuthzClient.create() calls CryptoIntegration.init() which is a no-op if a provider was already set. In the Keycloak testsuite and any app with both on classpath, the initialization order decides the provider, making behavior depend on who initializes first. The selection is therefore not deterministic for this design.

findings.title: logger.debugf used with a non-constant format string
findings.body: The 'Ignored crypto providers' message is built as a string and passed as the format to debugf. Any '%' in class names would be misinterpreted as a format specifier. Use debugf with a format argument instead.

findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: order() was added as an abstract interface method. Any third-party or out-of-tree CryptoProvider implementation will fail to compile or load. A default implementation would avoid breaking the SPI contract.

findings.title: getKeyStore ignores the format's provider and uses KeyStore.getInstance without provider
findings.body: getKeyStore returns KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()) which uses the format name directly (e.g. 'PKCS12' or 'BCFKS' names) and may fail for formats not in the default JDK, while DefaultCryptoProvider uses format.toString() and BC provider. Inconsistent behavior with the other providers.

findings.title: Test only checks round trip of concatenated form, not DER correctness
findings.body: The test asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) == x, but never verifies that the DER output verifies against the original JDK signature or matches the JDK-produced DER. A symmetric bug in both directions would pass. It also uses the EC keypair generated with default curve without checking the curve matches the algorithm's expected size.
